title: Band offsets and stability of WSe$_2$/RuCl$_3$ van der Waals charge-transfer contacts
authors: Thomas S. Nielsen, Edvard Solbrekken, Christian Overby, Christian V-B. Fokdal, Alfred J. H. Jones, Zhihao Jiang, Chakradhar Sahoo, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Søren Ulstrup
abstract: The layered Mott insulator $α$-RuCl$_3$ induces degenerate hole-doping in two-dimensional semiconductors due to its large electron affinity, making it a promising charge-transfer material for establishing ohmic contacts in electronic devices. In order to assess the applicability and guide the design of devices incorporating RuCl$_3$ it is critical to determine the electronic structure and robustness of the band offsets that underpin the transport properties of semiconductors in contact with RuCl$_3$. Here, we apply micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to determine the electronic structure of single-layer WSe$_2$ contacted to RuCl$_3$ on hexagonal boron nitride substrates. We find that formation of a functioning WSe$_2$/RuCl$_3$ contact leads to a valence band shift of $(0.68 \pm 0.05)$ eV towards the Fermi energy in WSe$_2$. The charge transfer effect is challenging to observe as it depends sensitively on fabrication conditions such as solvent exposure, quality of interface encapsulation and heating of RuCl$_3$, imposing strict requirements on device design to attain high-quality contacts.
summary: This work uses muARPES to characterize the electrical contact formed between a 2D semiconductor (WSe2) and a layered Mott insulator ($\alpha$-RuCl3). The researchers found that forming this junction causes a measurable valence band shift, suggesting successful charge transfer for ohmic contact. Crucially, they highlight that achieving stable, high-quality contacts is extremely sensitive to the experimental handling procedures.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the electronic structure and robustness of band offsets at the interface between single-layer WSe2 and alpha-RuCl3 van der Waals charge-transfer contacts.
main_result: Contact formation induces a significant valence band shift of (0.68 ± 0.05) eV in WSe2, establishing an ohmic contact via hole doping. However, the charge transfer effect is highly sensitive to fabrication conditions and RuCl3 degrades upon heating.
method: Micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (muARPES) was employed to measure the electronic structure of the heterostructure in ultra-high vacuum.
model_or_system: The physical system is a van der Waals heterostructure composed of single-layer WSe2 contacted with alpha-RuCl3, which acts as a layered Mott insulator. The analysis focuses on charge transfer effects and band alignment at this interface.
key_observables: Valence band maximum (VBM) shift ($\Delta E_{ct}$), core level peak shifts, electronic structure mapping across the Brillouin zone.
important_parameters: Charge transfer magnitude (0.68 eV); Fermi energy relative to VBM; temperature/heating history during sample preparation.
main_assumptions: The charge transfer effect is assumed to be measurable via ARPES shifts, but its observation is critically dependent on minimizing environmental contamination and thermal stress.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band alignments showing the energy shift (Fig. 1), ARPES spectra confirming Mott insulating state and degradation upon heating (Fig. 2), and spatial maps/valence band dispersions comparing WSe2/hBN vs WSe2/RuCl3 contacts (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need to characterize contact interfaces, details the muARPES methodology applied to the WSe2/RuCl3 system, presents quantitative measurements of band shifts and charge transfer, discusses the limitations imposed by sample handling and material stability, and concludes with implications for device design.
why_interesting: While primarily experimental condensed matter physics, the study deals with Mott insulators ($	ext{RuCl}_3$) and interface electronic structure engineering, which touches upon correlated electron phenomena and emergent quantum states at boundaries.
